spec: Build an IoT telemetry backend. Devices are registered in a DynamoDB device registry. Devices post temperature readings to an ingest endpoint that stores them in DynamoDB; any reading above a per-device threshold publishes an alert to an SNS topic. Include endpoints to register devices, set a device's threshold, and return the daily minimum, maximum and average per device.

complexity.rationale: Per-device thresholds and daily aggregates coordinate two data entities with alerting.

congruence_checklist: Alert fires only above the per-device threshold
Endpoint returning daily min/max/average per device

plan.summary: A FastAPI service for IoT temperature telemetry. Devices are registered in a DynamoDB device registry with a per-device temperature threshold. Devices POST readings to an ingest endpoint; each reading is persisted in a DynamoDB readings table keyed by device and timestamp. When a reading exceeds the device's configured threshold, the service publishes an alert message to an SNS topic so downstream subscribers can react. Additional endpoints allow registering/listing devices, updating a device's threshold, and querying daily aggregate statistics (min, max, average, count) per device computed from readings stored for a given UTC day.

endpoints.purpose: Register a new device in the DynamoDB device registry with optional name, location and alert threshold (default applied if omitted).
List all registered devices from the device registry.
Fetch a single device's registry record including its current threshold.
Set or update the per-device temperature alert threshold.
Ingest a temperature reading for a registered device: validate the device exists, store the reading in DynamoDB, and publish an SNS alert if the value exceeds the device threshold.
List raw readings for a device, optionally filtered by a start/end ISO-8601 timestamp range.
Return daily minimum, maximum, average and count of temperature readings for a device for a given date (defaults to the current UTC day).
Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness.

data_models.name: Reading
fields: day: str (YYYY-MM-DD, derived for daily aggregation)

aws_resources.name: iot-devices
aws_resources.justification: Device registry table required by the spec; partition key device_id stores device metadata and the per-device alert threshold read on every ingest and written by the threshold endpoint.

aws_resources.name: iot-readings
aws_resources.justification: Stores every ingested temperature reading with partition key device_id and sort key timestamp, enabling per-device range queries that back the daily min/max/average endpoint.

aws_resources.name: iot-telemetry-alerts
aws_resources.justification: The ingest endpoint publishes an alert message to this topic whenever a reading exceeds the device's threshold, exactly as the spec requires.

aws_resources.name: iot-telemetry-app-role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the backend service least-privilege access to GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/Query/Scan on the two DynamoDB tables and sns:Publish on the alerts topic.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/iot-telemetry
aws_resources.justification: Log group for application logs of ingest activity and triggered alerts, giving operational visibility into the service.

assumptions: Temperatures are in degrees Celsius and thresholds are an upper bound: an alert fires when reading > threshold (strictly greater).
If a device is registered without a threshold, a default of 30.0 C is applied.
Readings for unregistered devices are rejected with HTTP 404 rather than auto-registering the device.
Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC; if the device omits a timestamp the server stamps the current UTC time on ingest.
'Daily' aggregation means a UTC calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD); the stats endpoint defaults to today when no date query parameter is supplied.

Aggregates are computed on read by querying the readings table for the day's timestamp range, rather than maintained in a separate rollup table, which is sufficient at the expected volume and keeps a single source of truth.

No Lambda or API Gateway is planned: the spec has no asynchronous worker or scheduled processing; alerting is a synchronous SNS publish from the request path, and the backend runs as its own service started by the harness.
No authentication is specified; endpoints are open, and device identity is taken from the request payload/path.
DynamoDB tables use PAY_PER_REQUEST billing for LocalStack compatibility and simplicity.
SNS topic subscriptions (email, SQS, etc.) are out of scope; the application only publishes to the topic.

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 5 files — FastAPI IoT telemetry backend with a decoupled storage layer. `storage.py` defines a `TelemetryStore` interface with two implementations: `DynamoTelemetryStore` (boto3 DynamoDB resource + SNS client, both honouring `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` and defaulting to us-east-1, with table/topic names from `DEVICES_TABLE`/`READINGS_TABLE`/`ALERTS_TOPIC_NAME`/`ALERTS_TOPIC_ARN` env vars) and `InMemoryTelemetryStore` for offline use. `app.py` exposes /health, POST+GET /devices, GET /devices/{id}, PUT /devices/{id}/threshold, POST /readings (validates the device, stores the reading with canonical UTC timestamp and derived day, publishes an SNS alert when temperature > threshold), GET /devices/{id}/readings (optional start/end/limit) and GET /devices/{id}/stats/daily (min/max/avg/count for a UTC day, defaults to today). Store access is a FastAPI dependency so tests override it. tests/test_app.py covers every endpoint plus error paths with the in-memory store, and exercises the DynamoDB/SNS code paths with hand-written fakes and monkeypatched boto3 — no network or LocalStack required. Only fastapi, uvicorn, boto3 and pydantic are used; lines stay under 120 chars, no secrets, no debug=True, no eval/exec/shell.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the IoT telemetry backend, one-to-one with the plan's aws_resources list.

Files:
- versions.tf: terraform block with required_version and hashicorp/aws pinned to ~> 5.0 (plus hashicorp/local ~> 2.4), and the aws provider with default_tags carrying project, managed-by, application and environment.
- variables.tf: region, project/app/environment tags, and defaults matching the plan's names (iot-devices, iot-readings, iot-telemetry-alerts, iot-telemetry-app-role, /cloudforge/iot-telemetry) plus 365-day log retention.
- main.tf: resources only for what the app uses.
- outputs.tf: table names/ARNs, LSI name, SNS topic ARN/name, IAM role and policy ARNs, log group name, KMS key ARN, region.

Resources and how each traces to the plan:
- aws_dynamodb_table.devices (iot-devices): PAY_PER_REQUEST, hash key device_id — device registry with per-device threshold.
- aws_dynamodb_table.readings (iot-readings): hash key device_id, range key timestamp, plus a local secondary index on `day` to back the daily min/max/avg endpoint without a scan.
- aws_sns_topic.alerts (iot-telemetry-alerts) with a scoped topic policy — the ingest path publishes threshold-breach alerts.
- aws_cloudwatch_log_group.app (/cloudforge/iot-telemetry) — application logs.
- aws_iam_role.app + aws_iam_policy + attachment (iot-telemetry-app-role) — least privilege: registry table gets Get/BatchGet/Put/Update/Query/Scan/DescribeTable, readings table gets Get/BatchGet/Put/Query/Scan/DescribeTable on the table ARN and its index, sns:Publish/GetTopicAttributes on just the alert topic ARN, logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents/DescribeLogStreams scoped to the log group and its streams, and KMS Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey on the single CMK. No "*" actions and no "*" resources in the role policy; the assume-role policy names a single service principal.

Security posture for Checkov: DynamoDB tables enable point-in-time recovery and server-side encryption with a customer managed CMK; the SNS topic sets kms_master_key_id; the CloudWatch log group is KMS-encrypted with 365-day retention. A single aws_kms_key (rotation enabled, 7-day deletion window, alias) plus a non-wildcard key policy (account root admin, logs service and sns service scoped to specific actions) supports all three — it exists solely to satisfy the encryption-at-rest checks for the planned resources.

LocalStack Community compatibility: only DynamoDB, SNS, IAM, CloudWatch Logs and KMS are used — no RDS/ECS/EKS/ElastiCache, and no Lambda or API Gateway, matching the plan's explicit assumption that the backend runs as its own service.
